description: Choose the target C/C++ language standard, enable or disable individual standards, and get warnings for features the selected standards do not support.
command.checkWorkspace: Check All C/C++ Files in Workspace
command.showAvailableRulesOnly: Show Only the Features of the Selected Standard
view.name: Standards
config.title: C/C++ Standards
config.cpp.target: Target C++ standard. Used for feature diagnostics, the status bar and IntelliSense sync. Must be an enabled standard; if it is disabled, the nearest enabled standard is used instead.
config.cpp.disabled: C++ standards that are disabled. Disabled standards cannot be selected as the target, and in `allEnabled` diagnostics mode the code is not required to compile with them.
config.c.target: Target C standard. Used for feature diagnostics, the status bar and IntelliSense sync. Must be an enabled standard; if it is disabled, the nearest enabled standard is used instead.
config.c.disabled: C standards that are disabled. Disabled standards cannot be selected as the target, and in `allEnabled` diagnostics mode the code is not required to compile with them.
config.gnuExtensions: Use the GNU dialects (`-std=gnu++17`, `gnu11`, ...) for compiler flags and IntelliSense, and do not report features that GCC/Clang accept as GNU extensions.
config.diagnostics.enabled: Report uses of language and library features that the checked standards do not support.
config.diagnostics.mode: Which standards the code is checked against.
config.diagnostics.mode.target: Only the target standard: report features newer than the target and features removed by it.
config.diagnostics.mode.allEnabled: Every enabled standard: the code must compile with all of them (useful for libraries that support a range of standards).
config.diagnostics.checkRemovedFeatures: Also report features that a checked standard removed (for example `register` in C++17 or `std::auto_ptr`).
config.diagnostics.evaluatePreprocessor: Evaluate `#if` conditions (`__cplusplus`, `__STDC_VERSION__`, feature-test macros, `__has_include`, `#if 0`) so that code compiled only for some standards is checked only against those standards.
config.rules: Per-rule settings, usually edited with the **Configure Rules** panel. Keys are rule ids such as `cpp20.coroutines`, or prefixes ending in `*` such as `cpp17.lib.*`. Values: `"default"` follows the selected standard, `"allow"` never reports the rule, `"forbid"` reports every use even if the standard supports it. An object `{ "state": "forbid", "severity": "error" }` also sets the severity. Exact ids take precedence over prefixes. A single line can be suppressed with a `// cppstd-ignore` or `// cppstd-ignore-next-line [rule ...]` comment.
config.rules.forbid: Report every use, even if the standard supports the feature.
config.diagnostics.ignoredRules: Rule ids that are never reported, e.g. `cpp17.lib.optional`. A trailing `*` matches a prefix.
config.diagnostics.ignoredRules.deprecat: Use `#cppStandards.rules#` with the value `"allow"` instead. Entries here are still honored.
config.diagnostics.exclude: Glob patterns of files that are not checked, e.g. `**/third_party/**`.
config.sync.cpptools: Write the target standards to `C_Cpp.default.cppStandard` and `C_Cpp.default.cStandard` of the Microsoft C/C++ extension when they change.
config.sync.clangd: Maintain a managed block in each workspace folder's `.clangd` file that adds `-std=` for C and C++ sources. Turning this off removes the block.
config.compilerFlagStyle: Compiler flag syntax returned by `${command:cppStandards.cppFlag}` and `${command:cppStandards.cFlag}` (usable in tasks.json and launch.json).
config.statusBar.enabled: Show the target standard in the status bar when a C or C++ file is active.
config.diagnostics.syntaxTree: Parse files with tree-sitter (bundled, WebAssembly) for more precise checks: syntax-aware detection of casts, lambdas, `if`/`switch` initializers, `auto` parameters and more; names made visible by `using namespace std`, `using std::name` and namespace aliases; functions the file declares itself are not taken for library functions; and rules that need the tree (C99 mixed declarations and variable-length arrays, K&R definitions, C++17 class template argument deduction, C++14 relaxed `constexpr`). Lines that do not parse, and files over 1 MB, are checked with patterns.
config.sync.cmake: Write `CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD`, `CMAKE_C_STANDARD`, `*_STANDARD_REQUIRED` and `*_EXTENSIONS` for the target standards into CMake Tools' `cmake.configureSettings` (workspace). Only the entries added by this extension are changed; they are removed again when this setting is turned off.
config.sync.conformanceWarnings: Add Clang warnings for code the selected standards do not accept to the synced tools: `-pedantic` (ISO dialects) and, when the code must compile with every enabled standard, `-Wpre-c++17-compat`-style warnings for each newer standard. Written to the managed `.clangd` block (`#cppStandards.sync.clangd#`) and to `C_Cpp.codeAnalysis.clangTidy.args` (`#cppStandards.sync.cpptools#`).
config.sync.clangTidyChecks: Enable the closest clang-tidy check for each forbidden core rule (for example `cppcoreguidelines-macro-usage` for forbidden macro constants). Written to the managed `.clangd` block (`#cppStandards.sync.clangd#`) and to `C_Cpp.codeAnalysis.clangTidy.checks.enabled` (`#cppStandards.sync.cpptools#`).
